name: first_pullback_after_trend_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: When NIFTY establishes a sustained directional move of 0.3%+ from session open (≈70+ spot points), large institutional TWAP/VWAP orders driving that move are typically only 40–60% filled — their remaining allocation actively bids on pullbacks. The first time price retreats to the 3-minute EMA (the institutional 'add' level visible on all algo screens), these resting orders absorb the counter-trend selling, and price snaps back in the trend direction within 30–90 seconds. This bounce is detectable at 5-second resolution because the EMA retouch-and-rejection creates a 2–4 bar basing pattern with increasing closes — we enter as the close re-crosses EMA in the trend direction, capturing the first leg of the institutional re-accumulation.

indicators.name: return_from_open
indicators.purpose: NIFTY trend magnitude filter. Original used 0.5% on high-beta individual stocks. NIFTY index has lower volatility (diversified, index smoothing), so 0.3% (≈70 spot pts) is sufficient to signal institutional directional conviction — it represents a full morning push that can sustain a continuation. Above 0.5% NIFTY moves tend to see mean-reversion rather than continuation, so 0.3–0.5% is the sweet spot.

indicators.name: ema_36
indicators.purpose: Pullback anchor = 3-minute EMA. Original used EMA(9) on 1-min bars = a 9-minute EMA. We compress to 3-min (36 × 5s) because our hold time is 30–120s — we need the trigger to reflect the CURRENT near-term equilibrium, not a 9-minute lagged level. At 5s bars, the 3-min EMA is the fastest smoothed level that institutional algos also reference (3-min is a common algo sampling interval). This is NOT blind 12x scaling — we deliberately chose a faster period because we're catching the initial bounce, not the full multi-minute recovery.

indicators.name: rsi_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute RSI overextension guard. Prevents entries where the 'pullback' is actually a reversal into deeply overbought/oversold territory. Original RSI(14) on 1-min = 14-minute lookback. We use 36 bars (3-min) to match our trade trigger speed — a 14-min RSI would lag too much at 5s resolution to detect the fast overextension that invalidates the pullback thesis.

indicators.name: vwap_session
indicators.formula: Cumulative VWAP from session open, reset each day
indicators.purpose: Directional confirmation. Original required close > VWAP for longs. On NIFTY, VWAP is the institutional benchmark — being on the trend side of VWAP confirms that the institutional flow is still directional, not already mean-reverting toward VWAP. Cumulative measure, no scaling needed.

conditions: return_from_open > trend_threshold (0.30% default) — bull trend established
first time price crosses EMA-36 downward AND then back upward (first pullback cycle only)
close > ema_36 on bounce bar — re-established above EMA after pullback
close > vwap_session — institutional benchmark confirms bull bias
rsi_36 in [rsi_min, rsi_max] (default 35–65) — not deeply overextended
buy_ce.confirmation: Bar close re-crosses above EMA-36 after having been below it (the bounce completion)

conditions: first time price crosses EMA-36 upward AND then back downward (first pullback cycle only)
close < ema_36 on bounce bar — re-established below EMA after pullback
close < vwap_session — institutional benchmark confirms bear bias
rsi_36 in [rsi_min, rsi_max] (default 35–65) — not deeply oversold
buy_pe.confirmation: Bar close re-crosses below EMA-36 after having been above it (the bounce completion)

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option pts (≈8 NIFTY spot pts at delta 0.5). If the first pullback bounce thesis is correct, the EMA should not be violated by more than 4–5 spot points — the institutional buying floor holds. An 8 spot point violation means the EMA has failed as support, the pullback is a trend reversal, not a continuation. For a 30–120s hold, typical counter-moves on NIFTY false bounces reach 6–10 spot pts — stop at 4 option pts cuts the loss before the full counter-move develops.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option pts (≈14 NIFTY spot pts at delta 0.5). First pullback continuations on NIFTY trend days extend 15–25 spot pts from the EMA retouch. Targeting 7 option pts captures approximately 50% of the median continuation leg, achieves 1:1.75 R:R vs the 4pt stop, and exits well before the second pullback zone begins (which would take momentum away from the trade).

filters.vix_filter: none — NIFTY trend pullbacks work in all vol regimes; high VIX doesn't invalidate the institutional 'add on dip' behavior
filters.time_filter: entry only 09:30–15:00 IST; 09:30 start allows 15 minutes for a meaningful trend to form from open
filters.volume_filter: none — NIFTY index volume is noisy at 5s resolution; EMA pullback geometry is the primary filter
filters.trend_filter: return_from_open > 0.30% (bull) or < -0.30% (bear) — primary trend qualification filter
filters.spread_filter: not applicable — limit order execution at candle close

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — first pullback edge degrades if market microstructure changes (e.g., faster algo fills that reduce the 'first pullback' dip depth)

adaptation_notes: Original traded top-20 Nifty50 stocks on 1-min bars with hold of 15–60 min. Adaptation drops all stock-specific elements (universe filter, spread filter, event filter, vol-adjusted sizing). EMA period compressed from 9 bars (9-min on 1-min) to 36 bars (3-min on 5s) — NOT a blind 12x scale because we hold 30–120s not 15–60 min, requiring a faster pullback detection window. RSI period similarly compressed from 14 (14-min) to 36 (3-min) for the same reason. Trend threshold reduced from 0.5% (equity) to 0.3% because NIFTY is a diversified index with lower single-day vol vs individual large-cap stocks. 'Pullback count == 1' logic preserved as a per-day state machine that fires once per trend direction.
weaknesses: On gap-and-go days NIFTY may gap 0.3%+ at open, establishing 'trend' immediately; the first pullback then happens in the first 5–10 minutes with shallow EMA setups that fail at higher rates
Algorithmic definition of 'first pullback' via EMA cross is sensitive to bar-level noise at 5s — a single anomalous bar can trigger the pullback flag falsely
On trending days that accelerate quickly, EMA-36 may lag so far below price that the 'pullback' never reaches EMA, generating zero signals despite a clear trend
